arxiv-1807-09128.title: How to estimate the entropy inside a Schwarzschild black hole
arxiv-1807-09128.creator: Thomas Schürmann
arxiv-1807-09128.description: Abstract We reconsider the interrelation between the Schwarzschild radius and mass of a spherical symmetric non-rotating and uncharged black hole. By applying the relativistic mass-energy equivalence, the area of the horizon is expressed independently of the Schwarzschild radius in terms of an occupation number operator corresponding to the underlying many-body system of the particles inside the black hole.

arxiv-2110-04974.title: Value-Function-based Sequential Minimization for Bi-level Optimization
arxiv-2110-04974.creator: Risheng Liu, Xuan Liu, Shangzhi Zeng, Jin Zhang, and Yixuan Zhang
arxiv-2110-04974.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Risheng Liu, Xuan Liu, Shangzhi Zeng, Jin Zhang, and Yixuan Zhang. Gradient-based Bi-Level Optimization (BLO) methods have been widely applied to handle modern learning tasks. However, most existing strategies are theoretically designed based on restrictive assumptions (e.g., convexity of the lower-level sub-problem), and computationally not applicable for high-dimensional tasks. Moreover, there are almost no gradient-based methods able to solve BLO in those challenging scenarios, such as BLO with functional constraints and pessimistic BLO.

arxiv-2205-13885.title: YouTubers Not madeForKids : Detecting Channels Sharing Inappropriate Videos Targeting Children Conference: 14th ACM Web Science Conference 2022; June 26–29, 2022; Barcelona, Spain Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3501247.3531556 ISBN: 978-1-4503-9191-7/22/06
arxiv-2205-13885.creator: Myrsini Gkolemi, Panagiotis Papadopoulos, Evangelos P. Markatos, Nicolas Kourtellis
arxiv-2205-13885.description: Abstract . YouTube is one of the most popular social media and online video sharing platforms, and users turn to it for entertainment by consuming music videos, for educational or political purposes, advertising, etc. In the last years, hundreds of new channels have been creating and sharing videos targeting children, with themes related to animation, superhero movies, comics, etc.

arxiv-2207-04612.title: Synergy and Symmetry in Deep Learning: Interactions between the Data, Model, and Inference Algorithm
arxiv-2207-04612.creator: Lechao Xiao, Jeffrey Pennington
arxiv-2207-04612.description: Abstract Although learning in high dimensions is commonly believed to suffer from the curse of dimensionality, modern machine learning methods often exhibit an astonishing power to tackle a wide range of challenging real-world learning problems without using abundant amounts of data. How exactly these methods break this curse remains a fundamental open question in the theory of deep learning.

arxiv-2209-13254.title: Identifying and Extracting Football Features from Real-World Media Sources using Only Synthetic Training Data Conference: Article; August, 2022; Synthetic Football Training Data CCS: Social and professional topics CCS: Software and its engineering Software creation and management
arxiv-2209-13254.creator: Jose Cerqueira Fernandes and Benjamin Kenwright
arxiv-2209-13254.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jose Cerqueira Fernandes and Benjamin Kenwright. Real-world images used for training machine learning algorithms are often unstructured and inconsistent. The process of analysing and tagging these images can be costly and error prone (also availability, gaps and legal conundrums). However, as we demonstrate in this article, the potential to generate accurate graphical images that are indistinguishable from real-world sources has a multitude of benefits in machine learning paradigms.

arxiv-2405-01354.title: Human-Robot Interaction Conversational User Enjoyment Scale (HRI CUES)
arxiv-2405-01354.creator: Bahar Irfan, Jura Miniota, Sofia Thunberg, Erik Lagerstedt, Sanna Kuoppamäki, Gabriel Skantze, André Pereira
arxiv-2405-01354.description: Abstract Understanding user enjoyment is crucial in human-robot interaction (HRI), as it can impact interaction quality and influence user acceptance and long-term engagement with robots, particularly in the context of conversations with social robots. However, current assessment methods rely solely on self-reported questionnaires, failing to capture interaction dynamics.

arxiv-2501-02127.title: How do Humans take an Object from a Robot: Behavior changes observed in a User Study Conference: International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction; December 4–7, 2023; Gothenburg, Sweden International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction (HAI ’23), December 4–7, 2023, Gothenburg, Sweden Price: 15
arxiv-2501-02127.creator: Parag Khanna, Elmira Yadollahi, Iolanda Leite, Mårten Björkman, Christian Smith
arxiv-2501-02127.description: Abstract . To facilitate human-robot interaction and gain human trust, a robot should recognize and adapt to changes in human behavior. This work documents different human behaviors observed while taking objects from an interactive robot in an experimental study, categorized across two dimensions: pull force applied and handedness.

arxiv-2505-07465.title: Close-knit relatives: reproducing galactic rotation curves with a two-component bosonic dark matter model
arxiv-2505-07465.creator: Jorge Castelo Mourelle, Nicolas Sanchis-Gual, José A. Font
arxiv-2505-07465.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jorge Castelo Mourelle, Nicolas Sanchis-Gual, José A. Font. Bosonic stars — hypothetical astrophysical entities — are generally categorized into two primary classes based on the nature of their constituent particles: Einstein-Klein-Gordon stars, made up of massive scalar bosons, and Proca stars, their vector “cousins”. Depending on the boson masses and field frequencies, these objects may exhibit properties of diffuse, massive structures, with sizes comparable to or even exceeding those of galaxies.

pmc-11918870.title: Nurses' Experiences of the Caring Role during the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Scoping Review of Qualitative Research
pmc-11918870.creator: Mary O' Regan-Hyde, Caroline Dalton-O Connor, Angela Flynn, Ashling Murphy, Vera J. C. McCarthy
pmc-11918870.description: Aims To synthesize the evidence on nurses' experiences of their caring role during the COVID-19 pandemic and identify emerging concepts that have affected nurses within the caring role in relation to (a) their professional lives and (b) their personal lives.

pmc-12603999.title: Biomedical Applications of Nanozymes: An Enzymology Perspective
pmc-12603999.creator: Vasily G Panferov, Xiaohan Zhang, Ka‐Ying Wong, Jung Heon Lee, Juewen Liu
pmc-12603999.description: Nanozymes are catalytic nanomaterials that transform enzyme substrates into their corresponding products, offering enhanced stability and a cost‐effective alternative to traditional enzymes. As nanomaterials, they possess unique physicochemical properties and catalytic mechanisms distinct from those of enzymes. Such differences have profound, yet often neglected, implications in biomedical applications.

pmc-12611400.title: Exploration of efferocytosis-related genes as potential therapeutic targets in endometrial cancer
pmc-12611400.creator: Huiping Zhang, Man Di, Shan Wang, Mingming Wei, Mingxia Jia, Zhuo Zhou
pmc-12611400.description: BackgroundEfferocytosis is involved in the occurrence and development of various malignancies, but its role in endometrial cancer (EC) remains unclear. This study aims to employ bioinformatics methods to identify potential therapeutic targets associated with efferocytosis-related genes in EC.MethodsTranscriptomic and clinical data of EC were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database. Efferocytosis-related genes were curated from published literature.

pmc-12852762.title: Risk of major adverse cardiovascular events with aripiprazole versus olanzapine, quetiapine, and risperidone in severe mental illness: a target trial emulation
pmc-12852762.creator: Alvin Richards-Belle, Naomi Launders, Sarah Hardoon, Kenneth K C Man, Neil M Davies, Elvira Bramon, Joseph F Hayes, David P J Osborn
pmc-12852762.description: Initiating aripiprazole as antipsychotic monotherapy rather than olanzapine, quetiapine, or risperidone, might prevent/delay major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) over the long-term in people diagnosed with severe mental illness. Using Clinical Practice Research Datalink data, we emulated a trial of aripiprazole versus olanzapine, quetiapine, and risperidone in 20,404 patients 2005–2014.

pmc-13096338.title: Direct oxidative carbonylation of methane to acetic acid via high-valent iron-oxo mediated water activation
pmc-13096338.creator: Haonan Zhang, Richard J Lewis, A Iulian Dugulan, Yang Li, Shuai Wang, Zhenxing Wang, Jianrong Zeng, Nicholas F Dummer, Yanyan Xi, Yunyun Li, Thomas E Davies, Mingbo Wu, Graham J Hutchings, Wenting Wu
pmc-13096338.description: Direct conversion of CH4 into value-added chemicals is impeded by the inert C-H bonds and inefficient C-C coupling. We report a spatially separated Rh-O-Fe active-site architecture that decouples CH4 and H2O activation through a high-valent-metal mediated radical mechanism, enabling selective CH3COOH synthesis.

pmc-13297380.title: The Otoacoustic Emissions in the Universal Neonatal Hearing Screening in China and India: An Update on the Asian States (2005 to 2025)
pmc-13297380.creator: Stavros Hatzopoulos, Ludovica Cardinali, Piotr Henryk Skarzynski, Giovanna Zimatore
pmc-13297380.description: Highlights What are the main findings? China has developed large-scale, system-integrated UNHS programs with high and stable coverage, whereas India shows predominantly hospital-based implementations with heterogeneous coverage and follow-up.OAE-based screening, particularly in combination with AABR, is effective in both settings, but loss to follow-up and variability in program structure remain major limitations. What is the implication of the main finding?

pmc-13348813.creator: Zaib Ur Rehman, Muhammad Jahandad Basra, Adnan Hassan Tahir, Zahid Manzoor, Shanhui Ren, Alia Afzal, Chunchun Meng
pmc-13348813.description: This paper examines the research output and impact of Veterinary Research Institutes (VRIs) of the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences (CAAS), namely Shanghai Veterinary Research Institute (SHVRI), Harbin Veterinary Research Institute (HVRI), and Lanzhou Veterinary Research Institute (LVRI), to answer research questions.

pmc-13393800.title: Breaking bone-associated tumor vicious cycle through macrophage membrane-camouflaged nanodecoys for sonodynamic/epigenetic therapeutics of oral squamous cell carcinoma
pmc-13393800.creator: Mingxin Cao, Nan Zhou, Chuiyin Wang, Yang Xu, Xinming Li, Lei Sui, Yinsong Wang, Yue Wang, Xiaoying Yang
pmc-13393800.description: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is an aggressive tumor that metastasizes frequently and invades the maxillary or mandibular bone easily when adjacent to the jaw bone. Caused by tumor-induced osteoclasts activation, bone invasion could release various cytokines from bone matrix that further promote cancer progression, leading to a bone-associated tumor vicious cycle and poorer prognosis.

pmc-13519448.title: Hybridization-based gold nanoprobe assay for the detection of candidemia in ICU patients - A novel method
pmc-13519448.creator: Anitha Subramanian, Anupma Jyoti Kindo, Renuka M.K, Anusha Karunasagar
pmc-13519448.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Candidemia is a life-threatening infection in ICU patients, with mortality rates of 35-75%, yet current diagnostic methods such as blood culture and conventional Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) lack the sensitivity required for timely detection. Therefore, it is of interest to address this unmet diagnostic need, we developed a hybridization-based gold nanoprobe (AuNP) colorimetric assay for the direct detection of Candida DNA from 3 ml EDTA blood samples.
